default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t1-p1.vietnamese:
Recently, I have begun to find it enjoyable to do a little of something every day.

For example, I study English conversation, write essays, and, although I am clumsy at it, try knitting simple items.

When I say “a little every day,” it is not necessarily because I do not have enough time. Sometimes it is because I am not very good at something, so I can only do it little by little.

As I get older, there are times when I also find joy in making an effort to do something.

Things I once thought, when I was young, that I would probably never be able to do in my entire life gradually become reality when I try them. It is wonderful how amazing life is.

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t11-p1.vietnamese:
These days, I think quite a few people are considering changing jobs.

If you are seriously thinking about changing jobs, you should first try to organize your thoughts clearly by asking yourself what you really think about yourself.

One method is to write down all the reasons why you want to change jobs.

Changing jobs means giving up your current position and starting over at a new company.

Naturally, quite a few people may also experience a pay cut.

Therefore, before beginning a concrete job search, if you are dissatisfied with your current company, try to think about the reason for that dissatisfaction.

For example, some people may want to change jobs because, despite working very hard, their supervisor does not appreciate them and their stress continues to build. Others may have achieved the highest sales results but been transferred to a department they did not want.

However, although some people may have decided on their next company and be full of hope, problems involving human relationships will certainly exist wherever they go.

Therefore, try to consider objectively whether the dissatisfaction you currently have is truly serious.

Even so, if you still genuinely want to change jobs, begin your job-search activities in earnest.

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t12-p1.vietnamese:
Every year, Prefecture A conducts a 「Book-Reading Survey」 of high school students in the prefecture, and it recently announced this year's results.

According to the announcement, the percentage of students who had not read a single book during the month reached 55.1%, an increase of 1.8 percentage points over the previous year's survey.

The survey was conducted by questionnaire among 47,945 students at public and private high schools. By gender, 12,814 male students and 11,693 female students had not read any books.

Although these figures had declined for both males and females over the past few years, compared with the previous survey, the figure rose by 0.7 points for males and 3.0 points for females, meaning that the increase was greater among females.

As for the reasons for not reading, the most common answer was 「Because I prefer magazines and comic books」 at 35%, followed by 「Because using mobile phones and computers is more fun」 at 30%.

In addition, 20% of students answered, 「Because I am busy with schoolwork, cram school, homework, and so on」.

This suggests that the emergence of new media, together with the amount of time taken up by studying and club activities, is causing an increasing number of students to move away from printed books.

From now on, we may need to make an effort to teach students about the benefits and enjoyment of reading.

(Note) Moving away from printed books: No longer being interested in or attracted to books and newspapers.

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t13-p1.vietnamese:
The cold winter has ended, and April has arrived, bringing beautiful cherry blossoms.

April marks the beginning of a new school term, so the children have probably moved on to middle school or advanced to a new grade.

They have new classes and new friends, and they must be full of energy as they go to school every day.

My nephew has also started middle school. He does not seem to be used to his new routine yet, but he told me about something that happened one day.

During lunchtime, one student accidentally forgot to bring a lunch box.

When they saw this, all the classmates immediately shared small portions of the rice and food from their own lunches and ate together.

When I heard this story, I was deeply moved by the children’s thoughtful and warm concern for one another.

These days, there are convenience stores nearby almost everywhere, so even if the student had forgotten their lunch box, it would have been easy to buy another meal.

Therefore, there would have been absolutely no problem if the children had not shared their lunches.

However, the children in this class had a precious kindness that money can never buy.

I am sure this will become a wonderful class.

I think the mothers who prepared the lunch boxes would also feel happier making lunches every day if they knew about this.

Keep it up, children!

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t14-p1.vietnamese:
The spicy-food boom that began in Japan last year still shows no sign of cooling down.

Restaurants continue to introduce new menu items with twice the usual level of spiciness.

Because spicy food makes you sweat while eating it, it feels as though stress is quickly released.

It also seems to leave the mind feeling refreshed and lighter.

However, problems frequently arise as well.

Many people suffer stomach pain after eating spicy food and have to go back and forth to the bathroom.

There are also other concerns.

People often say that eating spicy food for a long time is bad for the stomach, but is this really true?

In conclusion, there is no need to worry to that extent.

The reason is that humans perceive spiciness not as a taste but as a sensation of pain.

Spicy compounds such as “capsaicin” and “allicin” disappear from the body within 2 to 3 days, so there is no concern that these compounds will accumulate in the body and cause problems.

However, that does not mean spicy food is good for everyone.

People with weak stomachs or intestines, and patients with high blood pressure, should preferably limit their intake of spicy food as much as possible.

Although spicy food is not a direct cause, it may indirectly worsen the symptoms of an illness, so great care is necessary.

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t15-p1.vietnamese:
We have entered an age of convenience in which we can communicate with just the touch of a finger.

However, is that really a good thing?

When I was young, each family had only one telephone.

Therefore, when I called a friend's home and a family member answered, I had to be careful about how I spoke, pay close attention, and learn how to communicate with someone from another generation.

I think what young people today—who are often said to be reluctant to interact with others—lack is practice of this kind.

Could the fact that they have had little experience since childhood with the tension or thoughtful consideration involved in interacting with others have led to the situation we see today?

Even when they have something difficult to say or need to change an appointment for personal reasons, they tend to settle the matter by email.

Even when they themselves should make a phone call, if no one answers when they call once, they may simply sit and wait for the other person to call back because the phone has a callback function, and this also concerns me.

At such times, I usually call the person directly and say: "The more difficult something is to say, the more important it is to convey it directly in words; only then can the other person feel your sincerity."

Because I always think that this is for the benefit of young people.

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t16-p1.vietnamese:
３月23日（水）くもり
March 23 (Wednesday) — Cloudy

I went to work at the office today as well.

I had planned to put my work aside before 4:00 and go shopping at the mall, but by the time I finished, it was already 6:00.

There was nothing else I could do, so I stopped by a nearby convenience store, bought a few things I needed for my trip, and went home.

When I got home, I found an email from the hotel I had booked online yesterday.

I thought I had booked a package including two nights, breakfast, and dinner.

However, I could not clearly understand the details in the automatic confirmation email, so I tried emailing the hotel directly to ask about it.

While I was at it, I also asked them to arrange a taxi from the station for the day I arrived.

３月24日（木）はれ
March 24 (Thursday) — Sunny

When I checked my email this morning, I saw that they had replied thoroughly.

The room had been booked according to the package I wanted, and they had also arranged the taxi for me.

They had even thoughtfully asked which day I wanted to have dinner and what time I would like to taste the wine included in the package at the wine cellar.

I was already beginning to feel excited before the trip had even started.

There was just one thing that concerned me.

Apparently, the hotel employee who emailed me thinks I am a man.

My name is Yuko, so foreigners often mistake me for a man.

I hear that in European names, girls’ names often end in "A," while boys’ names often end in "O."

Taxi driver, please remember to look for a Japanese woman at the station!

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t17-p1.vietnamese:
This happened when I traveled to Kyoto last year.

Just after I passed through the ticket gate at the station, I saw someone selling sweets and offering samples.

The sample was soft and delicious, so after discussing it with my son, I decided to buy some as a gift for my grandfather.

After paying inside the stall and preparing to leave the shop, I heard the sampling clerk talking on the phone.

It seemed that she was reporting to her company, saying, "As soon as I said there were only a few left, I made a sale."

Was she not talking about me? It is true that I partly bought them because she told me, "There are only a few left."

I intended to say something to the clerk, but decided not to.

I spent the day with an uncomfortable feeling of resentment in my heart, and then went to the hotel to check in.

At the front desk, I was given a postcard.

It was a message from an employee of the travel agency who had helped me, saying, "It is such a shame about the previous trip. I am so glad that you were able to set off safely this time."

The trip I had planned for May had been canceled because of a personal matter on my part, causing trouble for the travel agency.

Nevertheless, receiving such a warm message made me feel much more relieved.

I will continue to use their services for my next trip as well.

Both souvenir shops and travel agencies depend on their customers.

If the clerk had looked around the shop before making the phone call and recognized us, surely what she said would have been different.

I think she lacked consideration and sensitivity toward the customer.

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t18-p1.outline.3.label: The author's opinions and recommendations

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t18-p1.vietnamese:
This happened last Friday.

Wanting to read a book suddenly, I went to the library near my home at around 4:00 p.m. for the first time in a long while.

From the outside, the library had previously appeared brightly lit, but that day the lights were inexplicably off, making it look as though the library were closed.

I thought, “That’s strange.”

When I went inside, I was extremely surprised.

Perhaps because of the recent trend toward saving electricity, the inside of the library was far too dark.

Even in such a dim space, many people were reading, while students were studying on their own.

People had gathered around the places where the curtains were open and light from outside came in.

Wasn’t this practically telling people, “If you borrow a book, go home and read it. Study at home, too”?

Could this really be called a library?

I put up with it for a while, but when the sun set, I felt I had reached my limit. Just as I was about to leave, the lights came on.

When I looked at the clock, it was 6:00 p.m. Although the lights had been turned on, it was still quite dark compared with before.

They would probably keep the lighting at this level until closing time.

It might not be so inconvenient during presentations, but I really cannot understand excessive electricity saving in a library, where people need to read the words right in front of them.

I sincerely hope they will make the lights brighter so that visitors can use the library comfortably.

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t19-p1.vietnamese:
Tanaka, an eleventh-grade student at a high school in Tokyo, changes into his gym clothes as soon as the last class ends each day.

He then walks around both inside and outside the school, collecting seemingly recyclable waste in garbage bags of about 60 liters.

His job is to take the bags full of recyclable waste to the processing site and sort them again by type.

The way he skillfully crushes the sorted beverage cans is impressive.

Recently, some high schools, recognizing the importance of character education, have begun counting students' participation in volunteer activities over a designated period during the year toward their achievements. The work of being a “recycling assistant” is also recognized as volunteer activity.

Tanaka exceeded the required number of volunteer hours last year, but he continues doing this work to this day.

When asked why, he said: “Actually, I started at first because of the required volunteer hours, but it is fun working with friends and teachers I like. Besides, it is good for the environment, so I decided to continue.”

Dear Mr./Ms. Kimura,

The mornings and evenings have become much cooler lately. I hope you are well.

Thank you very much for taking the time to visit me in the hospital the other day despite being busy.

Thanks to you, I was safely discharged from the hospital yesterday.

For now, I plan to rest at home for a while, but the doctor said I should be able to return to work next month.

I should really come to your home to thank you in person, but please forgive me for sending this letter first.

I look forward to your continued support.

Suzuki

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t20-p1.vietnamese:
As someone who was rather shy, I felt anxious when I graduated from elementary school and entered junior high school, wondering whether I would be able to get along with everyone. My homeroom teacher said this to me:

“People are not perfect by nature, so it is unavoidable that you will dislike someone. However, dislike them in such a way that they do not realize it.”

I was extremely surprised when I heard these words.

When I was in elementary school, my teachers always taught us that everyone had to get along.

Yet my junior high school homeroom teacher said that it was all right to dislike someone.

I felt as though I was being treated somewhat like an adult.

Disliking someone without letting them realize it sounds simple, but I think it is actually extremely difficult.

However, by doing so, the other person will not be hurt, and the atmosphere of the class will not be negatively affected, so I think it is very important.

I may be regarded as two-faced, but from now on, for my own sake, for the other person's sake, and for the sake of the entire class, I want to become someone who knows how to dislike others tactfully.

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t21-p1.vietnamese:
As everyone knows, when you type on a keyboard, romaji is converted into hiragana, and then into kanji.

However, recently I have noticed that I make more typing mistakes while writing documents, which puzzled me. It seems to be related to the computer at my workplace.

What causes these typing mistakes? One thing I realized is the difference between the computers I use at home and at work.

Even if I make a typing mistake on my home computer, it has a function that automatically corrects it into a proper sentence.

At first, I was delighted and used this function, but gradually it became something I took for granted.

Noticing a typing mistake with my own eyes and moving my fingers to correct it is troublesome. However, by repeating this process many times, my fingers seem to memorize how to type correctly.

In short, this process is essential for improving typing skills. But if the computer automatically corrects mistakes, we can never improve, and the mistakes become ingrained habits.

When I use a less intelligent computer to type a document, these typing mistakes seem to appear all over the screen at once.

If we think carefully, aren’t there many similar things happening elsewhere?

Today, life has become convenient because machines do everything for us. But precisely because of this convenience, human abilities seem to be declining. Am I really the only one who feels a little uneasy and concerned about this?

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t22-p1.vietnamese:
A newspaper for my child's school published an article saying, "I am worried about children who do not return greetings," and I completely agreed with it.

There are also children around me who clearly know me, yet when I say, "Hello," they merely glance at my face and walk past.

Many times I have wanted to call them back and scold them, but then I thought there would be no point and let it go.

I think that the extent to which one should greet an acquaintance may vary depending on each person's common sense, but when someone has greeted you and you do not respond, how are we ultimately supposed to understand that? I honestly cannot understand it.

However, because I do not want my own child to behave that way, I always teach my daughter to greet people properly whenever she meets them.

In fact, there is also a senior colleague at my workplace who pretends not to hear me whenever I say, "Good morning," or, "I'm leaving now."

Perhaps that person dislikes me. But is it really acceptable not to greet someone simply because you dislike them?

I dislike that senior colleague too, so does that mean I do not have to greet them either?

Even if someone you do not know at all says, "Hello," is it not an adult's courtesy to wonder who they are while replying, "Hello," to them?

As someone who takes the initiative to greet others and responds with a smile when someone addresses me with a smile, I truly cannot understand people who think it is acceptable to keep an expressionless face at all times.

At first glance, it sounds like a very polite message, doesn’t it?

But, um... no contact information has actually been left.

For customers who have ordered from us before, we already know their contact information, so this is fine,

but the customer probably firmly believes that they have left their contact information as well.

As a result, they may be thinking things like, “Why haven’t they called me back? They’re so irresponsible.”

However, do you think that calling a place again after leaving a message and receiving no response for a long time takes quite a bit of courage?

Some customers may be too hesitant to contact us again and therefore never get in touch.

I always call back customers who leave messages, so

if you do not hear back from us, please assume that there is some reason and do not hesitate to call us again.

A similar situation sometimes occurs with e-mail.

There are also quite a few cases in which I send several replies to the e-mail address entered in the contact-information field, but all of them are returned as undeliverable.

Among customers who wish to receive a reply by e-mail, some also provide a telephone number.

In such cases, we will proactively contact them by telephone,

but if you provide no information other than your e-mail address, we have no way to contact you again.

In such cases, please do not hesitate to e-mail or telephone us again.

Thank you for your cooperation and understanding.

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t24-p1.vietnamese:
There is a proverb in England: “If you want to be happy for a day, go to the barber.”

Indeed, getting a haircut feels refreshing and helps change one's mood a little.

Recently, one place where we often see this idea put into practice is the “Hair 1000” chain, whose slogan is “10 minutes, 1,000 yen, haircuts only.”

“Hair 1000” has opened many shops in crowded areas, but

there are certain locations where it is especially focused on opening shops.

They are next to restrooms in train stations, underground shopping areas, and shopping centers.

Normally, the most popular locations in stations, underground shopping areas, and shopping centers are

near busy entrances or near escalators, where people gather when going up and down.

In general, restrooms are often located in inconspicuous corners,

and they tend to give a dirty impression, so

these are not popular locations for hair salons or restaurants.

However, “Hair 1000” has opened many shops in precisely these locations.

Do you know why?

First, the rent there is relatively cheap.

In addition, there is another major reason.

So what is it?

The key lies in something that is always available in a restroom.

The answer is a mirror.

Everyone washes their hands after using the restroom, but

at that moment, when they look in the mirror,

“Maybe my hair has gotten a little long.

Now that I think about it, there’s a hair salon right next door where the haircut takes only 10 minutes.

If it only takes 10 minutes, I have enough time, so I might as well stop in and get a haircut”—

and quite a few people have thoughts like these.

It can be said that the company has accurately understood human behavior and psychology and skillfully applied them to its business.

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t25-p1.vietnamese:
The summer vacation season has begun again this year.

Since the break is as short as usual, many people are probably considering domestic travel, but

when roads and trains are crowded, rented CDs and DVDs are highly recommended items.

Nowadays, portable playback devices are sold cheaply,

so we can enjoy movies on the Shinkansen or in a car, which means

they are also highly recommended for families without young children.

At first glance, renting discs seems convenient, but

even nationwide chains generally do not accept returns at locations other than the store where the discs were rented.

Consequently, it is common for people to exceed the rental period while on a trip and have to pay an additional late fee.

At times like these, the Kitanoya chain began offering a convenient service called “Return by Mail.”

This service allows customers to return rented CDs and DVDs to any postal mailbox anywhere in the country.

The additional cost is only 100 yen for up to 6 CDs and DVDs in total.

“I used to feel bored when traveling from Tokyo back to Osaka to visit my family because there was nothing to do, but after I started using the Return by Mail service, I began watching DVDs and had a great time,”

and “It really is convenient that I can return the discs at any mailbox anywhere in the country,” users said, expressing their satisfaction.

To use the service, you only need to tell a staff member, “I would like to return them by mail,” when renting the products.

Using this service seems likely to make traveling a little more enjoyable.

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t26-p1.outline.1.label: Why one cannot feel sleepy and the cycle of sleep deprivation
default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t26-p1.outline.1.note: The passage explains that not feeling sleepy results from a changed biological rhythm. When people must wake early but cannot go to bed early, anxiety and sleep deprivation arise, increasing the risk of chronic insomnia.
default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t26-p1.outline.2.label: Ways to adjust one’s sleep rhythm properly
default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t26-p1.outline.2.note: Offers scientific advice for restoring a sleep rhythm: gradually adjust waking and sleeping times, limit daytime naps, avoid stimulating drinks in the afternoon, exercise before dinner, and avoid catching up on sleep all at once on weekends.
default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t26-p1.outline.3.label: The mistake of using alcohol to fall asleep more easily
default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t26-p1.outline.3.note: Analyzes why drinking alcohol may seem to make it easier to sleep but is actually ineffective and carries a risk of alcohol dependence.
default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t26-p1.vietnamese:
Recently, the number of people struggling because they cannot go to sleep early is reportedly increasing.

Only those who have experienced it can understand how difficult it is not to be able to sleep.

Although they tell themselves, "I have to sleep...," some people simply cannot fall asleep no matter what they do and end up staying awake until morning.

So why can they not sleep?

① Not feeling sleepy is not an illness.

This is because the sleep rhythm changes for various reasons, such as the season or the time of sunrise.

However, adjusting one's sleeping hours appropriately to match these factors is not at all easy.

For someone who is used to going to bed at 2 or 3 a.m., even if an important matter requires them to get up an hour earlier, going to bed an hour earlier is also very difficult.

② When this condition continues, people gradually begin to feel "sleep-deprived," and this anxiety makes it even harder for them to sleep.

If it lasts only a short time, it may not cause any problems, but continuing to live this way can quite possibly lead to chronic insomnia.

So, ③ what should one do to readjust one's sleep rhythm?

First, gradually shift the delayed sleep-wake cycle earlier, little by little.

At the same time, try as hard as possible not to sleep during the day.

In addition, do not drink coffee or soft drinks or eat chocolate in the afternoon.

Moderate exercise is also very good, but it should be done before dinner.

Some people try to make up on weekends for the sleep they lost during the week, but this habit is not good.

Even if you lose one or two days' worth of sleep, sleeping for about 8 hours is enough.

Some people say that they sleep well after drinking alcohol.

However, although alcohol may make you feel sleepy quickly, it prevents deep sleep and makes it very easy to wake up soon afterward, so it is not actually very effective and carries a high risk of alcohol dependence.

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t28-p1.vietnamese:
Kitano University Library User Guide

【Hours】

Monday–Friday, 9:00–18:00 (Closed on Saturdays, Sundays, public holidays, the year-end and New Year holidays)

【How to borrow books】

Bring the book you wish to borrow and your student ID to the counter. Faculty and staff members should bring proof of identity or a library user card.

＊Loans are accepted until 10 minutes before closing time.

＊If the material you need is currently on loan, you may reserve it. If you register at the counter, we will contact you after it is returned.

【Number of books and loan periods】

Students: 5 books (2 weeks)

Graduate students: 10 books (2 weeks)

Faculty and staff: No limit (1 month)

＊People from outside the university may not borrow materials, but they may read or photocopy them inside the library.

＊Dictionaries, reference books, magazines, newspapers, videos, music CDs, and similar materials may not be taken out.

【Returning books】

Return books at the counter before the due date.

＊If returning books after closing time or on a closed day, place them in the book-return box.

【Overnight loans】

Reference books and back issues of magazines (not the latest issue) may be borrowed from closing time until opening time on the next day the library is open.

【Contact information】

01-234-5678 (extension 123)

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t3-p1.outline.2.note: Shifts to the reason the author becomes sad and depressed: many insects appear where they live as the weather grows warmer. This supports Question 1.
default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t3-p1.vietnamese:
The cherry blossom season is almost here.

I can hardly wait to go flower viewing.

Every year I go flower viewing at the same park, but this year I found another interesting park, so I plan to try going there.

At the park I used to visit, the entire park would be filled with food stalls during the flower-viewing season. I could enjoy the festive atmosphere and appreciate the blossoms fully without having to carry anything with me.

Just thinking about it gradually puts me in a good mood.

However, I live in a place where insects appear in large numbers as soon as the weather gets warm, so my mood sinks whenever I think about being bothered by insects soon.

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t33-p1.vietnamese:
This summer, a power shortage is occurring nationwide.

Therefore, everyone must try to conserve energy not only in offices but also at home.

There is no need to think of it as complicated.

For example, with a refrigerator, if you open the door repeatedly, overfill it with food, or put hot items inside, the temperature inside will rise, causing it to use a great deal of electricity to cool down again.

By doing simple things like these, we can save approximately 960 yen worth of electricity each year.

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t35-p1.vietnamese:
I never imagined that my fourth-grade daughter could make Japanese so interesting to me.

Last night, while I was making shredded egg to put in chilled somen noodles, she came over and said excitedly:

“That, that! You’re putting it in the somen, right, Mom? I really like this dish. What is it called?”

“It’s called kinshitamago (shredded egg),” I replied.

“Huh? What? So we can’t eat it?”

I thought she was joking, but she had an extremely serious expression on her face.

A little later, I was laughing hysterically in the kitchen, practically jumping for joy.

It turned out that she thought it meant “forbidden eggs” (kinshi is a homophone of a word meaning forbidden).

(Note 1) Chilled somen: a Japanese noodle dish.

(Note 2) Shredded egg: a dish made by frying a thin omelet and cutting it into long, thin strips.

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t37-p1.vietnamese:
The other day, something serious happened at a movie theater.

Because my right wrist was broken, I could not move my hand properly, and I dropped the mobile phone from my jeans pocket into a Western-style toilet.

Naturally, the phone was damaged and could no longer be turned on.

The phone contained a great deal of important data, such as work emails and customers’ contact information.

It was only after dropping it into the water that I realized how deeply the phone is the lifeline of modern life.

People regularly back up data on computers, but I doubt that many people go that far with their phones.

Fortunately, after I dried it with a hair dryer, the phone was able to turn on again.

Because of this incident, I signed up for my mobile carrier’s contact backup service.

I now periodically store my phone numbers, email addresses, and so on with the carrier.

“Don’t put all your eggs in one basket” is a phrase often used in risk management.

Modern phones have so many functions and are extremely convenient. It was only after dropping mine into the water that I realized I had inadvertently put all kinds of “eggs” into it.

It was a valuable experience that made me truly understand the “risk of excessive convenience.”

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t38-p1.vietnamese:
Yesterday I met a man named Watanabe.

He used to work for a large company in Tokyo, but was forced to leave his job in March and was looking for another job. After reconsidering, however, he applied for a government-supported agricultural training program for urban residents.

Young people’s attitudes toward agriculture seem to have changed greatly recently. When Mr. Watanabe applied, the competition was reportedly so fierce that 120 people applied for only 8 places.

Mr. Watanabe said, “Unlike the life of a salaried employee, the appeal of agriculture is that you can do everything with your own hands. After completing the training course, I plan to become a professional farmer.”

Young people returning to rural areas do not just farm; they also work on marketing at the same time, pursuing a form of “idea-driven agriculture” to maximize efficiency. Local governments struggling with aging populations and labor shortages are also actively holding agricultural information sessions for unemployed young people.

The number of consultations at agricultural information sessions, which was only 31 last year, rose to 60 in February and 80 in March this year. Of these, 80% of those seeking advice were reportedly between 20 and 40 years old.

However, some people are concerned that agriculture is difficult work for those without basic knowledge or experience, and that without careful consideration, it could become yet another failure.

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t39-p1.outline.4.note: Volunteering can bring much joy and new discoveries when continued over the long term at one's own pace without forcing oneself.
default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t39-p1.vietnamese:
Volunteering originally means “being a volunteer.”

The term refers to activities in which anyone willingly does what they can do, cooperates with the people around them, and receives no payment.

If you are thinking about volunteering, try looking around you for something you can do and that would be easy for you to do.

You do not necessarily need special knowledge or skills. I think there are activities that allow you to make use of your existing interests, work experience, or the things you enjoy.

Once you decide to participate in an activity, look carefully around you and think about what you should do.

In volunteer activities, courage and initiative are very important.

That is because if you simply sit and wait, no one will come to direct or order you around.

Gather your courage and boldly give it a try.

There, you will surely discover a new side of yourself and a different world.

However, there are also things we need to keep in mind.

Volunteering is absolutely not about “doing someone a favor.”

Rather, we are “partners,” living together as fellow human beings on this Earth.

It is taboo to pity others or regard them as unfortunate.

Help them from an equal perspective, as friends and fellow human beings.

Volunteering is an activity through which, if you continue over time, you can experience many new things and much joy.

Do not push yourself too hard; continue at your own pace for the long term.

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t4-p1.outline.1.label: The nature of redundant expressions
default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t4-p1.outline.1.note: Points out that the examples all involve unconsciously using the same meaning twice, a phenomenon known as 重複表現. This supports Question 1.
default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t4-p1.outline.2.label: The cause and the psychology behind the emphasis
default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t4-p1.outline.2.note: Explains that repetitive expressions stem from people's desire to emphasize what they want to convey.
default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t4-p1.vietnamese:
Even in Japanese, which many people use as a matter of course, there are many inaccurate expressions.

For example, “the very first” (一番最初) and “Happy New Year” (新年明けましておめでとうございます).

When written out, both use two words with the same meaning twice.

Do many people unconsciously blurt out such redundant expressions?

Why are redundant expressions used so frequently?

Perhaps they are intended for emphasis.

If we think carefully about “the very first,” “first” does not inherently have a first or second place. Yet the common human tendency is to believe that adding “very” makes the meaning more emphatic.

Location: 5th floor, Yamamoto City Cultural Center

How to register: Fill in the required information on the application form and submit it in person at the reception desk on the first floor of the main building. You may also register through the website.

Dates: July 1 (Monday) ～ August 30 (Friday)

Registration period: June 1 (Tuesday) ～ June 20 (Thursday)

Class schedule

Judo: Mondays & Thursdays, 18:00～19:00, 5,000 yen, 20 participants

Ikebana: Wednesdays & Thursdays, 10:00～11:00 / 19:00～20:00, 6,000 yen, 15 participants

Origami: Tuesdays & Fridays, 9:30～11:30 / 19:30～21:00, 5,000 yen, 15 participants

Tea ceremony: Mondays, Wednesdays & Fridays, 17:00～18:00, 4,000 yen, 15 participants

Japanese: Tuesdays & Thursdays, 14:00～15:00 / 20:00～21:00, 5,000 yen, 10 participants

＊Please note

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t41-p1.vietnamese:
I think it is really difficult to change something once we have become accustomed to it.

Right – left – right.

Ever since I was little, I was taught to check both sides when crossing a road or using a crosswalk.

My body—or perhaps my mind—does it automatically, even before I have time to think.

After graduating from university, I went to the United States to study English, planning to stay for two years.

Right – left – right. Cars drive on the opposite side here from Japan, but my head still moves exactly as it did before.

About six years have passed, but I am still in the United States.

Right – left – right. The fact that I step forward and then suddenly realize my mistake is exactly the same now as it was six years ago.

Two years ago, I was in a traffic accident and became unable to walk on my own.

As a result, I now live my life in a wheelchair.

Because my parents are quite wealthy, I have as much money as I need. However, as someone with a physical disability, I have no way to spend it, and I am going through lonely days.

I used to have a romantic partner, too, but after the accident, the people around me gradually drifted away. That was when I first realized that money is not everything.

Even once or twice a month would be fine. If possible, would you become my friend?

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t45-p1.vietnamese:
Perhaps because of the worsening economy, the number of “100-yen shops,” which sell all kinds of things for 100 yen, has been increasing recently.

The range of products on sale is so much greater than before that it cannot be compared, and both the designs and quality have continued to improve. They can no longer be taken lightly.

It could even be said that we have entered an age in which we can manage our daily lives using only 100-yen goods.

Of course, I myself am also a frequent customer.

Therefore, whenever I need something, I tend to look for it at a 100-yen shop first.

However, I do not buy everything at 100-yen shops. I choose only products that I genuinely like and think, “This is exactly what I need!”

On the other hand, there are also products that seem expensive even though they cost only 100 yen, so you need to be careful.

My recommendations are small household items, food, and snacks.

Why not take my advice and give them a try?

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t46-p1.vietnamese:
One day, while I was having dinner after returning home from work, my daughter said she would give me a pair of shorts to wear in the cool weather for Father's Day.

I told her that would be nice, but asked if she could make it a tie this year instead.

As expected, her reaction was, “It's the age of Cool Biz, so why would you want a tie?”

That, however, is exactly why I want to receive a tie this year.

In the past, when Father's Day was mentioned, almost everyone gave a tie. But with the Cool Biz trend becoming popular, this industry must have suffered serious losses just when its sales were usually at their highest.

Whenever everyone across Japan moves in the same direction, there are surely people who are negatively affected.

For precisely that reason, I cannot give up wearing a tie this year either.

The essential point is saving electricity. All you have to do is avoid reaching for the air-conditioner switch out of habit.

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t47-p1.vietnamese:
I hate dogs. More precisely, I’m afraid of them.

When I was little, a friend once brought over a puppy that looked very cute. When I tried to pick it up, it bit me on the hand.

Another day, while I was playing ball alone in front of my house, a large dog suddenly came charging toward me. I was so frightened that I ran away.

The dog chased me, and I ended up running around the streets near my house at full speed, I don’t know how many times.

As I ran, I wondered whether my heart might stop and I might die.

Because of experiences like these, at some point, no matter how cute a dog is, my first reaction became, “Oh no, I’m scared!” before I could think it was cute.

What troubles me most is the existence of owners who assume that because their dog is adorable, everyone else will love it too.

Recently, a neighboring household started keeping a dog as well. The wife even takes the dog with her when she goes out to throw away the garbage.

In the morning, I look out from the second-floor window to make sure the woman is not outside, and only then do I take out the garbage at top speed.

People who cannot tolerate cigarette smoke have nonsmoking train cars and nonsmoking seats, so why aren’t people who are afraid of dogs protected as well?

If there were such a thing as a dog-free area, I would like to live there in peace of mind.

Higashi Sports Group is Japan's longest-established bicycle manufacturer and has specialized exclusively in bicycle production for 50 years.

The company is recruiting new employees for fiscal 2012 as follows.

◆ Job description

Mainly visiting bicycle dealers headquartered in Osaka Prefecture and conducting sales by telephone.

◆ Application requirements

Applicants need only have graduated from high school or above; men and women are welcome.

Because the job involves visiting dealers, a regular driver's license is required.

Applicants must be able to work at the head office in Minami City.

Because employees frequently prepare documents such as quotations, computer literacy is required.

◆ How to apply

Please send your résumé, with a photograph attached, by mail.

◆ Salary

Salary depends on experience; please discuss it directly with us. (*There is a three-month probationary period.)

◆ Contact information

Please contact us by telephone or email.

Recently, I am often asked whether studying abroad is advantageous or disadvantageous when looking for a job, but studying abroad involves both “losses” and “gains.”

Personally, I believe that what I gain is much greater.

However, whether to study abroad or not is a decision that each person must make for themselves.

Nevertheless, I believe that people who are not afraid of failure and dare to move forward despite the risks are the ones who can grow tremendously.

To those who are about to study abroad, I would like to offer my sincere encouragement and support.

(Note 1) Yell: a cheer or encouraging words of support.

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t6-p1.vietnamese:
“Mama-tetsu” is a compound of “mama,” meaning mother, and “tetsu,” meaning railway. It refers to mothers who like railways or are railway enthusiasts (otaku).

However, mama-tetsu specifically refers to mothers who gradually become railway enthusiasts while buying railway picture books and toys for their children or taking them to see trains. Women who were already railway enthusiasts before becoming mothers or before having children are not called mama-tetsu.

Incidentally, women in the latter category—those who were already railway enthusiasts—are reportedly called “Tetsuko.”

(Note) Otaku: A person who is highly enthusiastic about a particular field and collects products and information related to it.

default.p.8nd_dokkai_n3-t7-p1.vietnamese:
Water is something we drink, wash our faces with, and use for cooking almost every day.

Tap water is said to have become tastier recently thanks to advances in technology, but with a few simple tips, we can make it taste even better.

First, the key is to draw tap water at night in advance.

This means that, compared with the morning, there are fewer impurities in the water at night after households have used a large amount of tap water.

Next, it is said that if you boil the water you have drawn in a kettle for about 5 to 6 minutes, even the very small amount of undesirable components remaining in the tap water will disappear.

In addition, if you chill it in the refrigerator, even tap water will become tasty enough to enjoy.

default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t1-q1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (d) 不思議なものだ。
The author expresses wonder at the mystery of life: things that seemed impossible when they were young gradually become reality.
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t1-q1.explanation: The key evidence is the final sentence of the passage: 「若い時は一生自分にはできないだろうけど、できたらいいなあと思っていたことが、ちょっとずつ実現したりもするから、人生って（不思議なものだ）。」 The complete sentence means: "Things that, when I was young, I thought I would never be able to do in my lifetime, but wished I could do, gradually come true, which is why life really is a mysterious and wonderful thing." Grammatically, 「na-adjective + なものだ」(here, 不思議なものだ) expresses deep wonder or amazement at an interesting phenomenon or truth of life. To avoid the trap in choice (c), remember that「〜た方がいい」is used to give someone advice about what they should do, so it does not fit after the topic「人生って」(as for life...). In addition, choices (a) and (b) both have negative, pessimistic meanings, which completely conflict with the cheerful, positive emotional flow of the passage, as shown by「楽しくなった」and「喜びを感じる」.
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t1-q1.why.0: ✗ (a) This choice is incorrect because the passage focuses on the excitement of making steady efforts, not on describing life as a difficult burden.
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t1-q1.why.1: ✗ (b) This choice is incorrect because the author embraces everything optimistically and does not complain that life consists entirely of difficulties.
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t1-q1.why.2: ✗ (c) The pattern 「〜た方がいい」 is used to give advice about what someone should do, so it does not fit the context of expressing feelings about life.
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t1-q1.why.3: ✓ (d) This choice is correct because it fully expresses the speaker's amazement and delight at the wonder of life as an apparently impossible wish gradually becomes reality.
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t10-q1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (c) 伝統の方法でお菓子を作る会社で大阪にある。
The advertisement clearly says that this is a traditional confectionery shop in Kyoto (京都), not Osaka (大阪), so this statement is incorrect according to the passage.
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t10-q1.explanation: The relevant information appears immediately in the opening sentence: 「当店は京都の和菓子屋としてはまだ若い会社ですが、伝統の作り方を守りながら、いつも新鮮なお菓子を作り、お客様にその味でご満足いただこうと努力してきました。」 (Although our shop is still a young company for a Kyoto wagashi store, we have worked to preserve traditional methods while always making fresh sweets and satisfying our customers with their flavor.) The key N3 grammar is 「Noun + としては」, used to make an assessment or comparison from a particular standpoint, status, or standard. It carries a relative nuance, comparing the subject with the general norm—in this case, implying that 30 years is still young compared with Kyoto brands that have existed for hundreds of years. Choice (c) is a subtle trap. Its first clause, "making sweets using traditional methods," matches the passage's 「伝統の作り方を守りながら」, but the test deliberately changes the location from Kyoto (京都) to Osaka (大阪). For reading questions asking which statement does not match the passage (合っていないもの), split each choice into smaller clauses and compare them independently, paying special attention to proper nouns such as place names and to numbers, which are often changed in the second half of a choice.
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t10-q1.why.0: ✗ (a) This information is consistent with the passage because the store clearly states that this year marks the 30th anniversary of its founding (創業30周年).
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t10-q1.why.1: ✗ (b) This matches the passage because the special discount program runs for only 10 days, from January 20 to 30.
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t10-q1.why.2: ✓ (c) This is the answer to choose because the passage introduces a bakery in Kyoto (京都), not Osaka (大阪).
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t10-q1.why.3: ✗ (d) This statement is completely consistent with the passage because the store offers a 30% discount on all products (全商品).
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t11-q1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (d) 転職したい理由を紙に一つずつ書いてみること
According to the passage, anyone who is truly serious about changing jobs should first organize their thoughts by writing down, one by one, the reasons they want to change jobs.
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t11-q1.explanation: The basis is the sentence: 「本気で転職を考えているなら、まず自分で自分のことをどう思っているのかを一度きちんと整理してみなければなりません。なぜ自分は転職したいのかをすべて紙に書いてみるなどの方法があります。」 (If you are seriously considering changing jobs, you must first try to organize your thoughts about yourself properly; one method is to try writing down on paper all the reasons you want to change jobs.) Grammatically, the author uses 「V-てみる」, in which the te-form combines with みる to mean “try doing something” in order to assess the situation, together with the obligatory pattern 「～なければならない」. This emphasizes the need for self-reflection before making a major decision. The adverb 「まず」(first) is also the key word corresponding directly to 「最初にすること」(the first thing to do) in the question. An important test-taking tip is not to fall for the vocabulary trap in answer choice (a): in this context, 「整理」means organizing abstract thoughts, not physically tidying a desk, furniture, or surrounding space.
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t11-q1.why.0: ✗ (a) The passage discusses reorganizing one's thoughts, not cleaning up one's desk or the surrounding space.
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t11-q1.why.1: ✗ (b) The author recommends clarifying why you want to change jobs, not looking for a job that suits you.
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t11-q1.why.2: ✗ (c) The passage contains no information whatsoever about discussing the matter with a senior colleague at the company or asking them for advice.
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t11-q1.why.3: ✓ (d) This choice accurately reflects the advice in the passage: try writing down all the reasons for wanting to change jobs in order to organize your thoughts.
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t11-q2.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (a) 場合によっては、もらえる金が少なくなることもある。
The author points out that changing jobs can naturally result in cases where one’s pay decreases, meaning the amount of money received may become smaller.
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t11-q2.explanation: To identify the risk associated with changing jobs in the passage, we rely on the sentence: 「当然、給料が下がるケースも少なくありません。」(Naturally, there are also quite a few cases in which salaries go down.) The key N3 grammar point is 「〜少なくない」, the negative form of 少ない, which softly affirms that something occurs fairly often. This corresponds to choice (a), 「V-る + こともある」, expressing that something may occasionally happen. The author paraphrases the risk of a salary reduction, 「給料が下がる」, as 「もらえる金が少なくなる」. A key reading-comprehension tip is to be careful with choices that reuse vocabulary from the passage, such as (c), which contains 希望, or (d), which contains 営業成績, but distort the context into “dangerous work” or “poor performance” to mislead the reader.
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t11-q2.why.0: ✓ (a) This choice is correct because the passage clearly mentions the possibility that in some cases wages may be reduced (給料が下がる), meaning that the amount received may be lower depending on the circumstances.
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t11-q2.why.1: ✗ (b) This choice is incorrect because the passage only mentions that interpersonal relationship problems (人間関係の問題) can occur anywhere; it does not say that the person was disliked by coworkers at their former company.
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t11-q2.why.2: ✗ (c) This choice is incorrect because the passage only gives the example of being transferred to a department against one’s wishes. It does not mention the possibility of having to do dangerous work.
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t11-q2.why.3: ✗ (d) This choice is incorrect because the author only gives the example of someone with top sales results (営業成績はトップだった) being transferred to another department; the passage does not say that poor performance led to dismissal.
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t11-q3.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (c) 転職の理由が適切なのかよく考えてみてからした方がいい。
The author advises readers to objectively examine and carefully consider the reasons for their dissatisfaction with their current company before actually starting to look for a new job.
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t11-q3.explanation: In option (c), the author uses `V-てから` (the て-form plus から), indicating that one action should be fully completed before proceeding to the next, together with the advice pattern `V-た方がいい` (the た-form plus ほうがいい), which recommends choosing an action because it is better in the specific situation. The complete meaning is: “You should think carefully about whether your reason for changing jobs is justified, and then decide whether to change jobs.” The key evidence comes from the original sentence: 「ですから、自分がいま持っている不満は、深刻なものかを客観的に考えてみましょう。」 (“Therefore, let us objectively consider whether the dissatisfaction we currently have is truly serious.”) An important JLPT reading strategy is to be cautious with extreme, absolute options such as 「いいことばかり」 (“nothing but good things” — sentence a), 「全然ない」 (“not at all” — sentence b), or 「〜しかない」 (“there is no choice but to ...” — sentence d). Authors generally view issues from multiple perspectives and offer careful advice rather than one-sided assertions.
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t11-q3.why.0: ✗ (a) This is incorrect because the passage says that changing jobs can lead to a lower salary and other difficulties, not that it is entirely beneficial and therefore worth doing hastily.
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t11-q3.why.1: ✗ (b) This is wrong because the author does not completely reject changing jobs; the author still supports beginning a job search if, after careful consideration, one still wants to change jobs.
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t11-q3.why.2: ✓ (c) This is correct because the author repeatedly emphasizes the need to reflect independently and consider the seriousness and validity of the reasons for dissatisfaction before taking action.
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t11-q3.why.3: ✗ (d) The author states that interpersonal problems exist in every environment, so changing jobs cannot necessarily solve them.
default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t12-q1.verdict:

default.q.8nd_dokkai_n3-t26-q2.explanation: The connective expression 「こうなると」 consists of the demonstrative 「こう」, which summarizes the situation just mentioned, and the dictionary-form verb 「なる」 followed by 「と」, expressing an inevitable condition: “once this happens, the following consequence results.” The preceding sentence is: 「なぜなら、いつも午前２、３時に眠りに入っていた人が、大事なことがあって１時間早く起きなければならなくなったからといって、１時間早く寝るのは難しいからである。」 It uses the N3 pattern 「～からといって」 (plain form + からといって: “just because... does not necessarily mean...”) and translates as: “Because someone who is accustomed to going to bed at 2 or 3 a.m. will find it difficult to go to bed an hour earlier merely because an important matter requires them to get up an hour earlier.” Thus, getting up earlier while going to bed at the same late time results in less total sleep. Learners may be misled by (d), where the phrase “sleep deprivation” appears nearby. The key is that the demonstrative 「こう」 always refers to the situation that forms the premise in the immediately preceding sentence, not to the result in the following clause.
